memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Do not rule over them ruthlessly, but fear your God'" - Lev 25:43 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A short verse with a sharp edge. Those who had authority over others were
warned not to use it ruthlessly. And once again the safeguard is not a human
regulator but reverence for God: fear your God.

Power reveals character. It is easy to be gentle when we have no advantage
over someone. The test comes when we do have the advantage — when someone
depends on us, works under us, or cannot easily push back. What do we do
with that power?

Dear friend, God is deeply concerned with how the strong treat the weak. He
repeatedly warns those with authority against harshness. The reason given is
striking: fear your God. The person under your authority may not be able to
call you to account, but God can, and He will.

Jesus turned the world's model of leadership upside down. He said the rulers
of the nations lord it over people, but it must not be so among you; whoever
wants to be great must be a servant (Matt 20:25-28). He Himself, with all
authority, washed His disciples' feet.

Wherever you hold power — as a parent, employer, leader, or simply as the
stronger party in a relationship — that power is a trust from God. Use it to
serve, never to crush.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do I use the power and authority I have over others?
2. Am I gentler in public than in private with those under me?
3. Where could I lead more like a servant this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, wherever You have given me authority, keep me from ruthlessness.
Teach me to lead as a servant, using every advantage to bless rather than to
crush. Amen.
